lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: operations in scientific notation

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A processor performs 6 × 10^9 operations per second. How many operations does it perform in 5 × 10^2 seconds? Write the answer in scientific notation.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A cell has a diameter of about 3 × 10^-2 meters. A virus has a diameter of about 6 × 10^-6 meters. How many times as large is the cell as the virus?
A student simplifies 8^6 × 8^3 as 8^18. Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: The exponents should be added, not multiplied: 6 + 3 = 9, so the product is 8^9.
The claim is correct; 8^18 is the product.
The bases should be multiplied together first.

items.prompt: A student multiplies (6 × 10^-5) × (6 × 10^0) and writes 36 × 10^-5. Which statement best analyzes the claim?
choices: The value is correct but not in scientific notation; 36 × 10^-5 should be rewritten as 3.6 × 10^-4.
The claim is correct and already in scientific notation.
The coefficients should have been added, not multiplied: 12 × 10^-5.
The exponents should have been multiplied: 36 × 10^0.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.
